correctness.rationale: Every depth-four code corresponds to a full ordered binary tree, enumerated bijectively by the recursion T_h=1+T_(h-1)^2, giving 677 trees through height four and 651 at exact height four. Each decoder has at most 15 proper-prefix states. Full-mask breadth-first search exhausts all reachable nonempty subsets, so first singleton distance is the exact shortest word length, and no singleton proves nonsynchronization. Independently written Python and C++17 programs reproduce identical full histogram (632 synchronizing, 19 nonsynchronizing), sharp maximum 17, and two extremizers; shortest witnesses simulated.

value.rationale: The newly published general bounds only locate the sharp height-four optimum in [17,33], whereas this complete height-four classification closes that natural first unresolved finite cutoff, counts the exact residual unsynchronizing cases, and supplies a full reset-threshold spectrum useful as a benchmark for larger heights. It is an exact finite structural boundary, not a code-only minor numerical perturbation; the known two-depth extremizers are not presented as new.
